input.question: If HIV is a retro virus, why can't we find a way to stop reverse transcriptase from working?
input.ground_truth: We do! [Reverse-transcriptase inhibitors](_URL_0_) are a class of anti-retroviral drugs that operate as you suggest. But we tend to see the same problem in highly targeted drugs acting on a disease that mutates easily (like HIV or cancer). The disease gains resistance to the drug by acquiring slight changes in the shape of the target protein.

Now, scientists want to stop this magic tool so the toy box can’t open and make more toy boxes. But it’s really tricky! The magic tool is hidden inside the toy box, and it changes its shape a little bit every time, so it’s hard for the scientists to make something that can always stop it.

It’s like trying to catch a slippery fish with your hands—it keeps wiggling away! That’s why it’s hard to stop reverse transcriptase from working every time. But the scientists are still trying their best!
